avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both increase bleeding risk through antiplatelet effects; indomethacin inhibits platelet aggregation and ginkgo interferes with platelet function
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or monitor closely for signs of bleeding (bruising, blood in urine/stool)

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects increase GI bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid therapeutic garlic supplements; dietary garlic is acceptable

avoid_supplements.name: Feverfew
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits platelet aggregation, increasing bleeding risk when combined with indomethacin's antiplatelet properties
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue feverfew or select alternative NSAID

avoid_supplements.name: ACE inhibitor supplements (e.g., potassium-sparing herbs)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal function and increase potassium retention; combined hyperkalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor serum potassium and renal function; avoid potassium supplements

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have antiplatelet properties and could slightly increase GI irritation risk
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased GI symptoms; generally safe at low-moderate doses

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effects may additively increase bleeding risk at very high doses
caution_supplements.action: Standard supplemental doses (≤2-3g/day) are typically safe; monitor for unusual bleeding

caution_supplements.name: Licorice root
caution_supplements.mechanism: May cause sodium retention and hypertension, compounding fluid retention from NSAIDs
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure and fluid status; limit duration of use

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (chronic/excessive use)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Both indomethacin and alcohol irritate gastric mucosa; synergistic GI ulceration and bleeding risk
avoid_foods.action: Strictly limit alcohol; avoid daily consumption and binge drinking

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal sodium excretion; excessive sodium may worsen fluid retention and hypertension
caution_foods.action: Maintain moderate sodium intake (<2,300mg/day); monitor blood pressure

caution_foods.name: Spicy foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May irritate gastric mucosa already compromised by indomethacin
caution_foods.action: Avoid excessive spicy foods if experiencing GI upset; take with food

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine may increase gastric acid secretion and GI irritation
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine intake; take indomethacin with food and adequate fluids

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function, blood pressure, and serum potassium regularly, especially in elderly patients or those with baseline hypertension/renal disease. Watch for GI symptoms (dyspepsia, abdominal pain, black stools) and signs of bleeding throughout therapy.
